status: concept proposal; not implemented as a playable biome
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: swamp biome concept for the existing medieval maths game.
Transform the supplied approved game concept into a SWAMP while preserving its exact visual language and the existing knight. The creative mood is Monty Python and the Holy Grail's wretched, absurd medieval comedy mixed with the dangerous bog-monster folklore and grim adventure of Moonstone: A Hard Day's Knight. These are mood references only; render everything in THIS game's approved woodcut style, never pixel art or cinematic fantasy painting.

INPUT: approved-concept-eyes.png is the edit target and strict style/character reference. Keep the same shabby, skinny, hunched knight on the left, facing right: closed dented bucket helmet, tiny black slit, battered short sword visibly held in his near hand, long split plank shield in the other, ragged faded dirty-orange cross tabard, thin patched armour, exact scruffy proportions and engraved print texture. Do not redesign him as a heroic muscular knight.

COMPOSITION: one wide 16:9 side-scrolling gameplay concept. Scene occupies upper 72–74%, horizontal muddy path at its bottom, matching thin distressed medieval divider immediately underneath with a tiny dirty-orange central diamond; lower quarter pale parchment with one large ornate carved equation reading exactly "9 + 6 = ?" in the game's black numerals with small orange inset strokes. No other words, captions, title, HUD or menus.

SWAMP ENVIRONMENT: the road is a narrow raised muddy bank through still black pools with broken engraved ripples and pale paper reflections. Crooked complete willow trunks with dangling moss frame the edges, roots gripping low tapered banks. Sparse reeds, a few mushrooms, exposed roots and rotten planks near the path, without covering the knight. Midground: a leaning ruined stone castle slowly sinking into the bog, one sagging wooden crossing, scattered clumps of bare trees. Far background: faint tree silhouettes separated by large unprinted parchment bands that imply ground mist. Airy gaps between clumps; a legible silhouette and distinct far, middle, near planes suitable as a future parallax reference, no continuous wall of detail. Whole objects with natural ends and ground tapering into sparse hatch marks, no rectangular sprite edges. Flat side view along the path, not an overhead view.

CREATURES: two clearly separated enemies to the right with space for combat. Closest, a stocky giant predatory toad, low and broad, with thick knuckled forelegs, warty engraved hide, a grumpy toothy mouth and a ludicrously inadequate dented cooking-pot helmet. Farther right, taller than the knight, an emaciated bog revenant with long crooked limbs, waterlogged ragged clothing, reeds caught in its hair, a crude long wooden pole with a rusted blade. Its face is an odd miserable medieval caricature, not an attractive cartoon and not a hollow demon. Small dark eye shadows with one tiny parchment-white dot each. A subtle huge half-submerged horned bog beast behind the distant ruins hints at a dangerous optional encounter; distant, subdued and barely revealed, never competing with the foreground. Original creature designs, tangible shabby materials, ominous but faintly ridiculous. No faces in bellies/shoulders and no explicit gore.

STYLE MUST MATCH REFERENCE: medieval black woodblock print on aged LIGHT parchment, irregular worn black contours, carved crosshatching and fine engraved detail at exactly the reference's density. Characters strongest ink; distant architecture/trees much finer and quieter. Warm neutral paper skin/interiors, charcoal grey ink, muted leather-brown, restrained dirty pale burnt orange mainly on the knight. Small earthy variations okay, but NO green/yellow tint over the image, no teal, violet or saturated accents. Opaque paper interiors in every character, tree and object, dark water made from print marks. No glossy wet surfaces, gradients, smooth shading, photographic lighting, 3D, Disney expressions or overworked ornament. Maintain the same detailed-but-readable balance and generous negative space as the original concept. One coherent finished concept illustration, not a contact sheet or sprite atlas.
notes: Requested mood: Monty Python mixed with Moonstone: A Hard Day's Knight, rendered in the existing game style.
